sections.h2: Where is West Linn, Oregon, and what shapes its terrain?
sections.html:
West Linn is a Clackamas County suburb on the bluffs between the Willamette and Tualatin rivers, directly across the Willamette from Oregon City. The city has 8.11 square miles in total, of which 0.68 square miles is water, and its elevation is about 679 feet.

Water and slope define the place. Willamette Falls is nearby, Mary S. Young State Recreation Area runs between Oregon Route 43 and the river with 5 to 8 miles of trails, and the Nature Conservancy’s 26-acre Camassia Natural Area sits in the middle of town.

For a seller, terrain matters in practical ways. The city’s planning page links a Water Resource Area Map and a Title 13 Habitat Conservation Area map, a flood plain approval application and a Natural Hazards Mitigation Plan. If your lot is wooded, steep or near a creek, those maps tell you what a buyer’s inspector may ask about.

West Linn started as a mill and river town. Major Robert Moore arrived in 1839 and bought about 1,000 acres from Chief Wanaxha in 1843, then platted a town he called Robin’s Nest. In 1845 the territorial legislature renamed it Linn City for Senator Lewis F. Linn.

A fire and the Great Flood of 1862 stopped growth in the early years. The Willamette Falls Locks and canal opened in 1873, the Willamette Falls Pulp and Paper Company began running in 1889, and the T. W. Sullivan Hydroelectric Plant opened the same year. Willamette incorporated in 1908, West Linn in 1913, and the two merged in 1916. The Oregon City Bridge was built in 1922.

The locks closed in 2011. The Willamette Falls Locks Authority, created in 2021, wants to restore them, and the Army Corps of Engineers owns them today. The city is a partner and financial contributor to that effort.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods make up West Linn?
sections.html:
West Linn has ten city-recognized neighborhood associations, organized under Chapter 2 of the municipal code, and its older areas began as separate townsites. An association’s boundaries can include more than one homeowners association, so a seller may deal with both.

  • Willamette. A former townsite that incorporated separately in 1908. The city also lists a Willamette Historic District, where Historic Design Review applies to landmarks and the district.
  • Bolton, Sunset and Multnomah City. Former townsites and developments that later joined the city.
  • Cedaroak, Marylhurst and Hidden Springs. Areas added through annexation.
  • Tanner Basin and Tannler. Infill areas created later.

Older neighborhoods often have larger trees, steeper driveways and homes from several eras on one street. Newer subdivisions carry HOA rules, so a resale certificate or rules packet may be part of the sale.

sections.h2: What do Census Bureau figures say about West Linn homes?
sections.html:
West Linn is one of the most owner-heavy and highest-income cities in the Portland area. The table shows the Census Bureau’s 2020 to 2024 estimates.

Higher values raise the bar for condition. Buyers shopping at those price levels often expect updated kitchens and systems, so a house that needs work can sit longer on the market. The 2020 census counted a median age of 43.1, with 17.9% of residents 65 or older. Many owners have lived in their homes a long time, and some now face a choice about repairs or a move.

sections.h2: What is the weather like in West Linn, and how does it affect a house?
sections.html:
West Linn has a wet, mild climate. Wikipedia’s climate summary puts annual precipitation at 44.37 inches, with January the wettest month at 6.78 inches. The mean daily high is 65 degrees and the mean daily low is 45.

Extremes still happen. The records are 107 degrees, set in 1956 and 1981, and minus 2 degrees, set in 1950. Moisture is the steady concern: moss on roofs, damp crawl spaces, clogged gutters and drainage on sloped lots all show up in inspection reports. Fixing them before listing can cost money and time, which is one reason owners with older houses consider selling as-is.

Nearly all of West Linn is in the West Linn-Wilsonville School District, which enrolled about 9,094 students in 2024 to 2025. The district’s West Linn schools include:

  • West Linn High School (opened 1919, about 1,724 students)
  • Athey Creek Middle School (1991) and Rosemont Ridge Middle School (1994)
  • Cedaroak Park, Sunset, Trillium Creek and Willamette primary schools

Willamette Primary opened in 1896 and Sunset in 1941, so two of the schools are among the oldest in the district. The district also reports that it phased out most middle school choice zones in 2025. Check your address with the district for the school your children would attend.

sections.h2: How do Clackamas County property taxes work for a West Linn seller?
sections.html:
Clackamas County bills West Linn property owners, and its 2025 to 2026 numbers show how large the base is. The county mailed 170,621 statements totaling $1,235,352,377, up 5.02%, across 130 taxing districts and 357 tax code areas.

The average single-family home had a real market value of $691,382 and a taxable value of $370,342, about 54%. The gap exists because Measure 50 caps assessed value growth at 3% a year unless the property changes.

The current year’s dates are:

  • November 16, 2026: full payment for a 3% discount, or two-thirds for 2%
  • February 16, 2027: second installment under the three-payment plan
  • May 17, 2027: final installment
  • December 31, 2026: last day to file a value appeal with the Property Value Appeals Board

Across the county, the median single-family home had a real market value of $595,816, and about 6.0% of properties paid tax on real market value instead of the lower assessed value. Measure 5 limits saved owners of about 12,300 properties $12.1 million in 2025.

A “yellow” statement means your lender asked for payment information and may be paying the tax. The county’s Assessment and Taxation office takes questions at 503-655-8671, and appeal forms go to the County Clerk, reachable at 503-655-8662.

sections.h2: What state tax rules matter when a West Linn house closes?
sections.html:
Oregon taxes become a lien on July 1, so the bill that comes out in the fall already covers a fiscal year that started before most buyers closed. If ownership changed after July 1, the fall statement may not show the new owner. Contact the tax collector for the amount if you have not received a statement by November 1.

Late interest is 1.333% per month under state rules, starting December 16 for the first installment. Title companies normally pay or prorate the tax at closing, but a seller who is behind should ask for a payoff figure before accepting any offer.

sections.h2: What parks, services and landmarks come with a West Linn address?
sections.html:
West Linn runs its own public library, which belongs to the Library Information Network of Clackamas County. Mary S. Young State Recreation Area and the Camassia Natural Area give the city large green spaces, and the Oregon City Bridge, built in 1922, links the town to the other side of the Willamette.

The Willamette Falls Locks stand as a local landmark even though boats no longer pass through them. The city identifies itself as a partner in the Locks Authority’s plan to reconnect the river communities. Mentioning nearby trails, the library and the school district in a listing or a cash conversation helps buyers see what the address offers.

sections.h2: How does selling West Linn property for cash compare with listing it?
sections.html:
A cash sale trades a higher possible list price for speed and fewer steps. Listing a West Linn house usually means preparing it, staging, showings, buyer financing and appraisal, and possible repair requests after inspection. A direct cash buyer purchases the house in its current state and the title company closes it.

Weigh the two on what you would net, not just the headline price. Count repairs, agent fees, months of tax, insurance and utilities, and any HOA dues while the house waits for a buyer.

faqs.q: Is West Linn in Clackamas County?
faqs.a: Yes. West Linn is in Clackamas County, and the county assessor and tax collector handle its property tax. The city sits across the Willamette River from Oregon City.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in West Linn?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimate is $770,200 for owner-occupied homes. It is a citywide survey number and does not value any single property.

faqs.q: When are Clackamas County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The current-year dates are November 16, 2026, February 16, 2027 and May 17, 2027. Paying in full on the first date earns a 3% discount.

faqs.q: Which school district covers West Linn?
faqs.a: Nearly all of the city is in the West Linn-Wilsonville School District. Its schools include West Linn High School, Athey Creek and Rosemont Ridge middle schools and four primary schools in the city.

faqs.q: Do historic rules apply to my West Linn house?
faqs.a: They can if the house is a historic landmark or in the Willamette Historic District, where Historic Design Review applies. Ask the city planning office at 503-656-3535.
